points.why: Says signed, traced loops show only internal consistency, that consistent is not true, and that a clean diagram tempts you to relax scrutiny.
Recommends having people who work where each link lives (support, CS, sales, product) defend each link and flagging any link nobody can defend, which matches the intent.
Treats the Fixes That Fail label as a separate claim and spells out the canonical test: a quick fix whose delayed side effect worsens the problem.
States directly that fluency is not correctness and that a polished output lowers scrutiny.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly refuses to accept the archetype label on the strength of correct polarities and requires naming the fix and its side effect.
